title: Malten AI News Network — 13 October 2026 — Marcus Reed
sections: Good morning. I'm Marcus Reed. Claire Bennett is off today, so I'll be bringing you the news. Welcome to Malten AI News Network for Tuesday, October thirteenth, twenty twenty-six. Today: world and American news, Baltimore updates, marathon achievements, and Baltimore's weather through Sunday.

The International Monetary Fund forecasts global economic growth of three point one percent this year. Artificial intelligence investment is supporting growth, but the Fund warns that Middle East conflict, expensive energy and rising borrowing costs threaten the outlook. In the Philippines, the Senate's impeachment court approved prosecutors' withdrawal of most charges against Vice President Sara Duterte. Meanwhile, Reuters reports that Rwanda has agreed to host Formula One racing from the early twenty thirties under a ten-year deal.

In American news, the Guardian reports that federal agents raided Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington home in an investigation involving alleged immigration fraud connected to her late father's paperwork. Omar calls the raid political intimidation. Democratic leaders condemned it. The allegations are not findings of guilt. In business, BlackRock's Investment Institute has turned neutral on U.S. stocks, citing artificial intelligence volatility, while favoring shorter-term Treasury securities.

Baltimore's Running Festival takes place Saturday, October seventeenth. About fifteen thousand runners are expected across the marathon, half-marathon, ten-kilometer and five-kilometer races. Drivers should allow extra time for road closures. The Banner also reports that Create Baltimore is promoting the city's welcoming environment to attract film and television productions. Financial incentives remain an important factor in studio location decisions.

Now sports. Kenya's Eliud Kipchoge won the Melbourne Marathon in Australia on Sunday, October eleventh. His time was two hours, nine minutes and ten seconds. He beat the previous race record of two hours, nine minutes and twelve seconds by two seconds. Australian Thomas Do Canto finished second, one minute and twenty-five seconds behind. It was Kipchoge's first marathon victory since Berlin in twenty twenty-three.

In Chicago, Kenya's Amos Kipruto won in two hours, one minute and nine seconds. Ethiopia's Hawi Feysa retained her women's title in two hours, thirteen minutes and thirty-three seconds. Kenya's Sharon Lokedi was second and Brigid Kosgei third. Clayton Young led the American men in two hours, five minutes and twenty-three seconds. Emma Grace Hurley led the American women in two hours, twenty minutes and forty-seven seconds, setting an American women's marathon debut record. Both Americans finished seventh overall.

Now Baltimore's forecast, prepared Tuesday morning. All temperatures are Fahrenheit. Tuesday: mostly sunny, high eighty-two, low sixty-three. Wednesday: warm and humid, with isolated late-afternoon thunderstorms possible; high eighty-seven, low sixty-one. Thursday: less humid, with sunshine followed by clouds; high seventy, low sixty. Friday: windy, with showers and thunderstorms; high eighty-one, low forty-nine. Some storms could produce damaging gusts.

Saturday: mostly sunny, breezy and cooler, with a high of fifty-eight and a low of forty. Sunday: partly sunny, high sixty, low forty-six. Secure loose outdoor items before the gusty weather. Running Festival spectators should prepare for a chilly Saturday morning. Forecasts can change, so check current alerts before heading out. Thank you for watching Malten AI News Network. Please subscribe to the channel for more broadcasts, and turn on notifications so you never miss an update. Have a safe and productive day.
